subject: Clarify per-request billing increments and long-context rounding
messages:
From: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@acme-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on how you bill long-context requests / rounding

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — very helpful. A few procurement questions came up when we ran the usage examples overnight and I want to make sure our finance team understands how Redwood will bill the calls we make. Short summary of our usage profile attached (acme_usage_examples.csv). A few concrete questions: 

- For requests that include a ~65k token context (we plan to use your long-context model), do you bill the entire input context + output tokens, or is there any prefix/KV caching or deduping that reduces billed tokens?
- Do you apply per-request minimums or rounding increments? Our ingestion pipeline often issues many small requests (~5–15 tokens each) and rounding up would materially change the economics.
- If we hit a cache (e.g., repeated calls over the same conversation), are cached tokens billed?
- For embeddings and reranking calls (very small token counts but a lot of requests), is there a different granularity or minimum charge?

Procurement would like a written confirmation of the exact billing rules we should put in our SOW/PO. Also can you confirm whether you offer one-token granularity for enterprise committed customers?

Appreciate the help — cc'ing legal (legal@acme-analytics.com).

Best,
Ethan
Head of Product Ops
Acme Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics Legal <legal@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on how you bill long-context requests / rounding

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear examples, and for sharing the CSV. Short answers up front, then I9ll loop in pricing to confirm a written term we can add to the SOW.

1) Long-context (65k) requests: billed = tokens processed by the model (input + generated output). If you use our prefix/KV cache feature and the request hits the cache, the repeated prefix tokens are not re-billed for that request. Practically: first time you populate the cache we bill those tokens; subsequent cache hits skip billing for the cached prefix.

2) Per-request minimums & rounding: default hosted pricing uses 1-token granularity with a soft per-request minimum of 3 tokens (this prevents micro-billing noise for tiny calls). However, some legacy volume tiers rounded small requests up to an 8-token block. For Enterprise commitments we can remove the per-request minimum and provide 1-token exact billing as a contractual term.

3) Cached tokens: see (1) — cache hits are not billed. Note: KV-cache eviction/warm-up can cause initial charges when the cache is populated.

4) Embeddings/reranking: billed per embedding call as input tokens + embedding unit charge (separate SKU). For very high QPS of tiny embedding calls we recommend batching on the client side or using our batch-embedding endpoint; for committed customers we can also provide adjusted granularity so you aren't rounded unfavorably.

I9m cc9ing Kar (“karthik_iyer@redwood.com”) on pricing to confirm the exact contract language and to propose the formal concession (1-token granularity + waive per-request minimum) if you proceed with the $40k/month committed tier you mentioned in the call. Marissa from Customer Success (marissa_cole@redwood.com) is looped for migration/implementation notes.

Let me know if you want a short call to walk through concrete invoicing examples.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick question on how you bill long-context requests / rounding

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Ethan9s email + my reply. Key asks from procurement: written confirmation of billing mechanics, and whether we can offer 1-token granularity + waive the per-request 3-token minimum as a concession for a $40k/month committed deal.

Can you confirm the precise language we should put in the SOW (particularly around cache behavior and the initial cache warm-up billing)? Also, if we agree to waive the minimum, any internal approval needed on the pricing/legal side?

Thanks — I9d like to propose the concession in writing to Acme today if possible.

- Vanessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick question on how you bill long-context requests / rounding

Vanessa — thanks for the summary. Confirming the billing behavior and approving the concession with precise contract language below. Feel free to paste this into the SOW.

Contract language (recommended):
- Billing unit: billed tokens = input tokens + generated output tokens actually processed by the model. Tokens are counted using Redwood9s standard tokenization and reported on invoices.
- Caching: Redwood9s prefix/KV cache reduces billed tokens on cache hits. Tokens stored in the cache are billed when initially written (cache warm-up). Subsequent requests that fully hit cached prefixes do not re-incur token charges for those prefix tokens. Partial cache hits are billed for the non-cached portions only.
- Granularity & minimums: default hosted customers are billed at 1-token granularity with a soft per-request minimum of 3 tokens. For enterprise committed contracts we will: (a) remove the soft per-request minimum, and (b) commit to 1-token granularity for all SKUs. These exceptions require a committed spend threshold (in this case: $40,000/month minimum commitment for the duration of the 12-month term).
- Long-context notes: very large contexts (e.g., 65k tokens) are billed only for tokens actually processed; overhead for attention/serving is not billed as additional token units. However, if the request triggers KV-cache population or material model re-compilation, customers may see distinct one-time charges related to initial workload shaping (these are operational events and we will notify customers).
- Embeddings & reranking: embeddings are billed under the embedding SKU (per-vector or per-token per the SKU). We will include standard language allowing batching recommendations; for enterprise tiers we can define an alternate embedding granularity where tiny calls are aggregated for billing purposes.

Internal approvals: legal has signed off on this wording as standard for enterprise deals; finance requests that we capture the committed monthly amount and term in the SOW/PO before waiving the per-request minimum. So yes — we can offer the concession for the $40k/month committed deal you mentioned.

One operational note: the billing system will show the cache warm-up charges in a separate line item ("cache population tokens") on the invoice for transparency.

Karthik
Head of Pricing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics Legal <legal@acme-analytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on how you bill long-context requests / rounding

Ethan — following up with the formal terms we can include in the SOW per Kar9s note below. I9ve attached a short term sheet that mirrors this language (redwood-billing-term-sheet.pdf).

To recap / confirm for procurement:
- Billing unit: input + output tokens, counted with Redwood tokenization.
- Cache behavior: initial cache population billed when written; subsequent cache hits not re-billed for cached tokens.
- Granularity & minimums: for Acme Analytics (DEAL-2026-003) we will remove the soft per-request 3-token minimum and provide 1-token granularity across text and embedding SKUs, contingent on a committed spend of $40,000/month for a 12-month term.
- Long-context: 65k-token requests will be billed for tokens processed; any operational one-time charges (cache population, large warm-ups) will be listed separately on the invoice as "cache population tokens" and communicated in advance.

Next steps: please review the attached term sheet and confirm you9re good with the $40k/month commitment and 12-month period. If so I9ll route a DocuSign and we can lock in the custom billing granularity on day one.

Attachments: redwood-billing-term-sheet.pdf (term sheet summary), acme_usage_examples.csv (your sample usage).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
